o.text: Borrowed from Persian چرکین (čerkin), from Persian چرک (čerk), from Proto-Common Turkic *čirik, from Proto-Turkic *čiri-.

glosses: brother-in-law, specifically, the brother of one's spouse

o.text: From Proto-Turkic *kādïn (“relative-in-law”), whence also qayınana (“mother-in-law”) and qayınata (“father-in-law”). Compare Turkish kayın (“in law”), Tatar каенага (qayınağa, “older brother of one's wife”), and каенэне (qäyenene, “younger brother of one's wife”).

Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish دلو (delü), from Proto-Turkic *tēlbe (“mad, stupid”). Cognate with Turkish deli, Uzbek telba, Turkmen däli and telbe, Southern Altai тели (teli), Tatar тилбә (tilbä, “foolish person”), Chuvash тилӗр (tilĕr, “become enraged”) etc.
From Proto-Turkic *yulduŕ (“star”), whence also Azerbaijani ulduz. See more at Turkish yıldırım.
Likely from Turkish açıklamak. By surface analysis, açıq + -la.
